clue.text: Nothing worried visiting Russian banker in involving just one party

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the nothing-and-worried letters sit within the river's name

parts.note: the Ural is a Russian river, and a river is a 'banker' because it has banks
nil means nothing, a zero score
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A Russian bank official, worried about getting nothing, acts on his own in some deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian banker' looks like a financier, but in crosswords a 'banker' is often a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A unilateral decision or action is taken by a single side without the agreement of others.

clue.text: Type of paint Barnstaple man energetically carries around

indicators.note: around tells us the carried letters are turned to read the other way
the phrase carries the answer within its letters, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A Devon man from Barnstaple lugs a tin of paint about with great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' signals letters held inside 'Barnstaple man energetically' (LEMANE); 'around' then turns them back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel paint dries to a hard glossy finish, a recognised kind of paint.

clue.text: Angers police officer requiring information leading to armed criminal

indicators.note: leading to places the information piece in front of what follows

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the word armed is rearranged

explanation.surface: A furious policeman needs details before tackling an armed criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angers' is not a verb but the city in western France, so the officer is French. 'criminal' rearranges ARMED to DARME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French national police force, as found in Angers.

clue.text: Keeping reserved seats unoccupied for lectures

indicators.note: keeping means the outer letters hold the next piece within them
unoccupied empties the word seats of its inside letters, leaving only its ends

parts.note: a reserved person is cold, aloof and distant

explanation.surface: Seats are held back and left empty for a series of talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lectures' looks like the noun but is the verb: to lecture someone is to tell them off.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone in the sense of rebuking them at length is to scold them.

clue.text: Head of government brought down gave a scowl

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to bring something down is to lower it

explanation.surface: A prime minister is toppled and pulls an angry face.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to stare angrily, which is the same as scowling.

clue.text: Yew, piece cut at intervals that's used for fencing

indicators.note: cutting the words at regular intervals keeps every second letter only

explanation.surface: A length of yew is chopped regularly for use as fence posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests garden boundaries, but it is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is one of the three swords used in the sport of fencing.

clue.text: Hardship in Cornish town not unknown

indicators.note: not means the unknown letter is to be absent from the town's name

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, England's far south-western county
z is one of the letters mathematicians use for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Life is hard in a Cornish town that has no unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: A penance is a self-imposed punishment or ordeal, so a form of hardship endured.

clue.text: In Cup red player, yard away, smashed upright

indicators.note: away means the yard letter is sent off from the pool of letters
smashed letters are broken up and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer in red is sent off in a cup tie and the team is crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes Y from IN CUP RED PLAYER, and 'smashed' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpendicular means at right angles to the horizontal, standing straight up.

clue.text: Song about love includes, on reflection, oddly soppy line

indicators.note: includes means the outer pair takes in the reflected piece

parts.note: ca, from circa, means about
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

indicators.note: reflection turns the letters back to front, as a mirror does
oddly keeps the first, third and fifth letters of soppy

explanation.surface: A love song that, thinking it over, is a bit soppy in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns the odd letters plus line into LYPS, which then sits between the 'about' and 'love' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean style of song, originally from Trinidad.

clue.text: Western Isles and Rum, Boris due there?

indicators.note: rum in the sense of odd or peculiar tells us these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Boris is expected on the Hebridean island of Rum, out in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like another Hebridean island but is the anagram signal, meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The Outer Hebrides are the Scottish island chain also officially called the Western Isles.

clue.text: Good example of English way to break record

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the pieces go within the record

parts.note: a roll is a list or register, a kind of record
a mode is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: An English approach to setting a new record is held up as exemplary.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person others look up to and copy, a good example to follow.

clue.text: Take away by force all others picked up

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on a radio, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the rest means all the others

explanation.surface: Seizing something while everybody else is collected.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest something is to wrench or seize it from someone violently.

clue.text: Group meeting cross, upset by European getting lavish praise

indicators.note: by places the European letter beside, here in front of, the rest
in a down-reading sense, upset means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
a cross is shaped like the letter X

explanation.surface: A meeting group gets cross and is upset by a European who gushes praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LOT + X back to front, giving XTOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly and enthusiastically, so to heap lavish praise on.

clue.text: Endlessly lie over runs on Irish bank

indicators.note: endlessly takes off the last letter of the word for lie

parts.note: to lie down is to rest

indicators.note: runs, as colours run, means the letters spread and shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps lying, over and over, about runs on an Irish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' rearranges OVER to ERVO. 'bank' is not a financial one but a store held in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a store or supply kept for later use, just as a bank holds a stock.

clue.text: Ordinary student interrupts important American right-winger as required

indicators.note: interrupts means the student letter breaks into the important word

parts.note: big means important, as in a big decision
l, from a learner driver's plate, stands for student
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: A regular student barges in on a powerful American conservative, as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obligatory is compulsory, i.e. required by rule or law.

clue.text: Evidence perhaps of defective heating in sleeping area and rodents

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
ice forming indoors would show that the heating had broken down

explanation.surface: Signs of a broken boiler in the bedroom, plus some mice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to picture a cold bedroom; reading the answer as two words (4,3) shows how frozen water in a dormitory fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small, mostly tree-dwelling rodents famed for long hibernation.

clue.text: Adolescent from Italy and male friend eating curry, keen to leave?

parts.note: i is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: eating means the friend word takes the curry remnant inside it

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: to leave says the keen word's letters go from the curry word

parts.note: curry is taken as the word itself before letters are removed
to keen is to wail or cry for the dead

explanation.surface: A boy from Italy and his mate eat a curry, eager to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' is not eager but to wail, CRY; taking C, R and Y from CURRY leaves UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescent can mean childish or not fully grown up, which is what immature means.

clue.text: Repeatedly discovered Hindus, all ages, creating humour

indicators.note: dis-covered, with covers removed, strips the outer letters from each word in turn

explanation.surface: Hindus of every age keep being found to create comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humour' is the verb, to go along with someone's wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour a person is to indulge them, giving in to their whims.

clue.text: Suggestion of union having struggle to adopt resolution

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the resolution piece goes inside
struggle suggests twisting and writhing, so the word union is rearranged

parts.note: an end is a resolution or conclusion

explanation.surface: A trade union, fighting hard, hints it may pass a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggle' rearranges UNION to INNUO, which takes in END. 'resolution' looks like a motion but means a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an oblique hint or insinuation, usually a suggestive one.

clue.text: South American doctor, rival occasionally, Costa Rican's ready to welcome

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the doctor and rival letters go inside

parts.note: the colón is the currency of Costa Rica, and ready is slang for cash
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: occasionally keeps only some letters, here the second and fourth of rival

explanation.surface: A medic and his rival are welcomed in Costa Rica, ready and waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is not prepared but money, so the Costa Rican currency, COLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A Colombian is a person from Colombia, a country in South America.

clue.text: Pressed co-chair on education squeezes

indicators.note: the phrase squeezes the answer between its word breaks, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A joint chair presses hard on the education budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are pressed have been smoothed flat with an iron.

clue.text: Posh replacement for that woman's aboard racehorse for business mogul

indicators.note: a replacement for something takes its place, so one piece swaps out the other
aboard tells us the pronoun is found within the horse's name

parts.note: Shergar was a famous Derby-winning racehorse kidnapped in Ireland in 1983
her is the possessive for that woman
U means upper class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A posh stand-in for a jockey's mount, to be owned by a tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar is the British entrepreneur behind the UK version of The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Sugar is a well-known British businessman, the host of the UK show The Apprentice.

clue.text: Arabic, say, that actor has to learn

definitions.meaning: Arabic is an example of a ..., a system of writing
the text of a play an actor memorises

explanation.surface: An actor must learn some Arabic for a role.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is both a writing system and the written text of a play or film.

clue.text: Border control

definitions.meaning: a boundary or edge, a border
to restrict or keep it under control

explanation.definitionFit: Limit is both a noun for an edge or boundary and a verb for restricting.

clue.text: Touch old volume this writer has penned

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the old volume sits within

parts.note: this writer is the setter speaking of himself, so me

explanation.surface: An old book I wrote is moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like written, but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch someone emotionally is to move them.

clue.text: Made too much of duty to conceal mistake in dictionary

indicators.note: in places the combined duty and mistake piece inside the dictionary

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the mistake goes within the duty

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a duty paid on goods in Britain
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A tax hides an error in the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' is a tax here, the British value added tax, not an obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overrated has been praised or valued more highly than it deserves.

clue.text: Gear extremely religious European always wears

indicators.note: wears means the outer piece puts the next one on, enclosing it
extremely takes the two extreme letters of religious

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A devout European always dresses in the same outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' looks like clothing, chiming with 'wears', but it is the car's backward gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverse is the gear in a vehicle used to drive backwards.

clue.text: Leaves band over dispute previously, is obliged to go

indicators.note: previously places the shortened dispute in front of the band piece
to go says the following pieces leave the word dispute

parts.note: put can mean compelled or obliged, as in being put to do something

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the band word reads backwards

parts.note: a strap is a band of leather or fabric

explanation.surface: A musician leaves the band after an earlier dispute, being forced out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' is not a group of musicians but a STRAP, which 'over' turns to PARTS. Removing IS and PUT from DISPUTE leaves DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place is to depart from it.
